impact:
T-008's gate reports a platform split as "linux = 69 passed / 2 skipped", but that figure comes from overriding `process.platform` in `spikes/platform.mjs`. That changes which tests RUN and nothing about the host — not the kernel's ephemeral port range, not `sun_path`'s limit, not filesystem or signal semantics. Review round 10 found a genuine Linux-breaking defect sitting underneath that green column: `publishAllocation` rejected any kernel-assigned port outside 49152-65535 (macOS's measured range), while Linux's default `net.ipv4.ip_local_port_range` is 32768-60999 — so a valid assignment of e.g. 45000 was refused and startup would have failed on a correctly configured Linux host. The simulation was structurally incapable of catching it.

That specific bug is fixed (the acceptance rule is now "any non-privileged port", pinned by a test acquiring port 40000) and the deliverable's portability section has been rewritten to claim only that the split routes tests correctly. But the underlying gap stands: no Linux host has ever run this suite. Anything else in the adopted primitive that depends on host behaviour rather than on Node semantics is unverified there by the same argument.

Consumers of this gate — T-010 (snapshot store) and T-011 (service single-instance guard + control-plane socket) — would otherwise inherit "verified cross-platform" from a document that cannot support it.

This is coupled to T-008 open question 2 (owner decision: must these prototypes pass on Linux, or is v0.2 macOS-only?), and it now has a concrete cost attached. If Linux is in scope, the gate's empirical evidence must be re-taken on a real Linux host — CI runner or container — not simulated. If v0.2 is macOS-only, that should be stated explicitly so the claim is scoped rather than assumed.
resolution: Folded into the v0.2 re-spec (the ISS-030 ticket rewrites) as a stated evidence boundary. The coupled open question (T-008 OQ2: must the prototypes pass on Linux, or is v0.2 macOS-only?) is settled by owner strategy N-001 (2026-08-01): macOS first, Windows and Linux later — so v0.2 is macOS-only by decision, and per this issue's own disposition the required action is scoping the claim, not re-taking evidence now. The deliverable already carries the scoping (docs/v0.2-prototype-findings.md: every measurement n=1 on macOS arm64/APFS/Node 22.18.0, 'Nothing below is claimed for Linux'; the portability section claims only that the platform split routes tests correctly and records that no Linux host has ever run the suite). The remaining inheritance hazard is exactly the tickets ISS-030 requires rewriting, so the re-spec carries this requirement: each rewritten ticket consuming the T-008 primitive (T-010, T-011, and T-012/T-013 where they reuse PortLock or the publish path) must state that its empirical basis is macOS-only and must not claim or imply cross-platform verification. Linux-milestone gate item, recorded here so it is not lost: before any Linux support claim, the T-008 spike suite must be re-run on a real Linux host (CI runner or container) with zero skips on that host — a process.platform simulation is structurally incapable of standing in, as the port-range defect proved. The one concrete Linux-breaking bug found (allocation port-range acceptance rule tuned to macOS's 49152-65535 vs Linux's default 32768-60999) is already fixed — the rule is now 'any non-privileged port' — and pinned by the deliberate port-40000 test.
title: v0.2 locking/socket evidence is macOS-only: real Linux verification never ran
